skeleton.finalText:
I wrote `src/index.ts`, and `npm run build` finished with no errors.

The contract is one class, because the spec describes stored state: how many questions each contributor has asked about each task today.

- **`QuestionLimiter`** takes a `Clock` (a function that returns a `Date`) when it is created. A test can control the time, for example by stepping from `2026-03-01T23:59:59.999Z` to `2026-03-02T00:00:00.000Z` for the midnight reset.
- **`remaining(contributorId, taskId)`** returns how many questions are left today and does not use one up.
- **`ask(contributorId, taskId)`** returns an `AskResult`. Its doc comment says it throws when either id is empty and that no allowance is used.
- **`AskResult`** is either `{ accepted: true; remaining }` or `{ accepted: false; remaining; message }`.

To set up a scenario like "has asked 19 questions today", a test calls `ask` that many times; there is no separate way to preload counts. The spec only says asking fails on empty ids, so `remaining` is not documented as throwing.

The build also created `src/index.js`. It's covered by `.gitignore`, and I didn't write it myself.

Exports: `Clock`, `AskResult`, `QuestionLimiter`

public.finalText:
I wrote the public test suite in `tests/public/question-limit.test.ts`. `npm run build` reports no errors. When run, every test fails with `not implemented`, as expected while the bodies throw.

Each of the spec's seven scenarios has a happy-path test and a boundary test:

| Scenario | Happy path | Boundary case |
|---|---|---|
| Full allowance | A new contributor/task pair reads 20, and reading doesn't use a question | Reading the count 25 times (more than the limit) still leaves all 20 questions |
| Accepted question uses one | The first question is accepted with 19 left; `remaining()` agrees | The first question at exactly `00:00:00.000Z` gives 19 |
| Twentieth accepted | After 19 questions, the 20th is accepted with 0 left | `remaining()` reads 1 before the 20th question and 0 after it |
| Twenty-first refused | It's refused with 0 left and the exact message from the spec | Further questions stay refused and the count never drops below 0 |
| Midnight reset | The spec's case: refused at `23:59:59.999Z`, accepted at `00:00:00.000Z` with 19 left | Questions at `00:00:00.000Z` and `23:59:59.999Z` count as the same day; the next day starts at 20 |
| Separate allowances | With c1/t1 used up, c1/t2 and c2/t1 are still accepted | ID pairs that would clash if naively joined into one key stay separate (e.g. `"a:b"`/`"c"` and `"a"`/`"b:c"`) |
| Empty ids | An empty contributor id, an empty task id, or both all throw | With one question left, 50 rejected asks use none of it; the 20th question is still accepted |

- **Fixed clock:** every test passes a hand-set clock that only moves when the test moves it, and nothing touches the network or filesystem.
- **Not tested:** the tests don't check what kind of error the empty-id case throws, or what `remaining()` does with empty ids, because the spec doesn't say.
- **Cleanup:** the build produced `src/index.js` and `tests/public/question-limit.test.js`. I deleted both, so the only file I added is the `.ts` test file.

14 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I've written the hidden suite in `tests/private/`. `npm run build` reports no errors, and all 47 tests fail against the current interface because the constructor throws `not implemented`.

To check the suite, I ran it in a scratch copy of the project against an implementation I wrote to the spec. It passed 47/47. I also ran it against five shortcut versions; each one passes some or all of the public suite, and the hidden suite catches all five:

| Shortcut | Public | Private |
|---|---|---|
| Day taken from local time instead of UTC | 12/14 | 35/47 |
| Day keyed on day-of-month only (`getUTCDate`) | **14/14** | 46/47 |
| Rolling 24-hour window instead of a midnight-UTC reset | 13/14 | 37/47 |
| Empty ids return a refused result instead of throwing | 12/14 | 42/47 |
| Ids joined into a key with `:` | 13/14 | 46/47 |

The day-of-month shortcut is the only one that passes the whole public suite; the hidden suite catches it by comparing the same date in different months and years. The `:` join is already caught by the public suite, so the hidden suite adds more separators on top of it.

What the hidden tests add beyond the public ones:
- **Local time zones:** a separate file sets `process.env.TZ` to Los Angeles, Tokyo, Kiritimati and New York, and restores it after each test. This catches implementations that work out the day in local time.
- **Midnight reset:** a late-day batch resets at 00:00 UTC even within 24 hours, and an early-day batch still counts at 23:59:59.999. A partly used day resets to 20, not to what was left. It also covers month, year and leap-day boundaries, skipped days, several days in a row, and every pair resetting rather than only the one that asks first.
- **Separate allowances:** pairs get full allowances of 20 and partial counts are tracked when asks are interleaved. Ids that could collide are checked: other separators, a null byte, JSON-style quoting, `__proto__`/`constructor`/`toString`, case, Unicode, surrounding whitespace and long ids.
- **Empty ids:** they throw an `Error` rather than returning a result, even when the pair is exhausted or on a new day. No pair loses any allowance.
- **Counting and refusals:** the count goes down by exactly one per question from 19 to 0, reads interleaved with every ask use nothing, and 50 refusals in a row never go below 0. A refusal for one pair doesn't use another pair's questions.

The spec names no error message for empty ids, so those tests only check that an `Error` is thrown and that no allowance is used.

I deleted the compiled `.js` files my builds produced in `src/` and `tests/`, which left them as they were before. The helper code is copied into each test file, because the rules require every file in `tests/private/` to end in `.test.ts`.

47 tests, in 2 files.

Open in the spec: none
